gloss: to soak in water; to immerse in water

definitions.gloss: to soak in water; to immerse in water
definitions.explanation: To place something in water and leave it submerged, typically for cleaning, softening, or preparation purposes.

examples.japanese: {米|こめ}を{水|みず}に{浸|ひた}す。
{豆|まめ}を{一晩|ひとばん}{水|みず}に{浸|ひた}しておく。
examples.english: To soak beans in water overnight.

examples.japanese: {乾燥|かんそう}わかめを{水|みず}に{浸|ひた}して{戻|もど}してから{使|つか}う。
examples.english: Soak the dried wakame in water to reconstitute it before using.

notes:
A very common cooking and daily-life expression. Soaking ingredients in water is a fundamental step in Japanese cooking.

COMMON USES IN COOKING:
- {米|こめ}を{水|みず}に{浸|ひた}す: soaking rice before cooking (typically 30 minutes to an hour)
- {豆|まめ}を{水|みず}に{浸|ひた}す: soaking dried beans
- {乾物|かんぶつ}を{水|みず}に{浸|ひた}す: soaking dried goods (shiitake, kombu, etc.)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {水|みず}につける: to put in water — very similar, slightly more casual
- {水|みず}に{漬|つ}ける: to soak/pickle in water — can also mean marinating
- {浸|ひた}す alone means "to soak" or "to immerse" and can be used with liquids other than water

USAGE:
{浸|ひた}す (transitive) vs. {浸|ひた}る (intransitive): {浸|ひた}す means to soak something; {浸|ひた}る means to be soaked or immersed.
